In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, characterization, and application of volatile metal- organic complexes as precursors for the MOCV D growth of high temperature superconductor, dielectric, and electro-optical thin films.
the development of new routes to high temperature superconducting films, lattice-matched insulators, and electro-optical materials for superconducting electronic devices.
the development of new synthetic routes to volatile metal-organic complexes for the CVD (chemical vapor deposition) growth and characterization of thin films of technologically important materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MOCVD approach to the growth of superconducting films and devices is a viable one and is being pursued by a number of groups worldwide.

the coordination chemistry of metal-organic precursors to high temperature superconducting materials has advanced to the point where the MOCVD route is a viable alternative to the more traditional solid state reaction methods for the preparation of thin films of the YBCO, BSCCO, and TBCCO phases.

the MOCVD growth of superconducting and other thin films from metal-organic complexes has now become a viable technology, with the capability of producing films with properties comparable to films prepared by other techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MOCVD growth of high quality thin films is possible for the YBCO superconductor, the YAl03, NdGa03 and PrGa03 dielectrics and for BaTi03 and Sr2MTOg electro-optic materials, but that the BSCCO and TBCCO superconductors and BaPbOg are still problematic.
the P-diketonates are the preferred precursors for YBCO and BSCCO growth, while the ketoiminates are the precursors of choice for TBCCO and the dielectric and electro-optic phases.
we can grow films with a variety of compositions, structures, and morphologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MOCVD process is a powerful tool for the synthesis of high quality thin films of these materials and that the choice of metal-organic precursor is a key factor in achieving the desired film quality and morphology.
the volatility of the metal-organic complexes is a key factor in achieving the highest quality thin films.

the volatility of the complexes and their ability to decompose in the vapor phase to yield stoichiometric films of the desired composition can be optimized by careful choice of the metal, ligand, and counterion.
